# Translations

What a field of a page or of a component reads in one of the site's other languages. The site's languages themselves are site.setLocales and site.setMainLocale (site, settings and domains).

[`translation.set`](#translationset)

## translation.set

Set or clear one translation: what one field of a page, or of a component definition, reads in one of the site's other languages. The main language is never translated: change its words with tree.set_text (or instance.setProp, page.setHead). A translation made now is current; one whose main-language value changes later reads as stale until it is set again. Refused: `op_target` (the pointer names no field with a value), `l10n.locale` (not one of the site's other languages), `l10n.target` (a field that is not translated), `l10n.shape` (a value the field does not take), `head.image` (a social image that is not a picture of the media library).

- **op**; class `content` (Content author, Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "translate", "language", "heading", "headline", "text", "words".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | { page: uuid } \| { component: string } | yes | Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |
| `locale` | string | yes | One of the site's other languages (site_context locales), never its main one: the main language is the tree itself. |
| `pointer` | string (max 400) | yes | A JSON Pointer to the field it translates. On a page: /tree/nodes/<nodeId>/text (or /runs) for a text's words, /tree/nodes/<nodeId>/alt or /src for a picture, /tree/nodes/<nodeId>/href for a link, /tree/nodes/<nodeId>/props/<prop> for an instance's text, link or picture prop, /tree/nodes/<nodeId>/attrs/<aria-label\|title>, /head/title, /head/metaTitle, /head/description, /head/ogImage. In a definition: its nodes the same way, and /props/<index>/default for a prop's default. |
| `value` | string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (string \| number \| boolean \| null \| …[] \| Record<string, …>)[] \| Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| …[] \| Record<string, …>>)[] \| Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (string \| number \| boolean \| null \| …[] \| Record<strin… (the whole schema: discover_operations with names) | yes | The value in that language, in the field's own shape (a text's words as a string, runs as runs, a media id for a picture); null clears the translation, so the field reads the main language again. |
| `src` | string |  | Leave it out: the translation is made from the field's current value in the main language (an undo states the hash it was made from). |
| `from` | string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (string \| number \| boolean \| null \| …[] \| Record<string, …>)[] \| Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| …[] \| Record<string, …>>)[] \| Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (string \| number \| boolean \| null \| …[] \| Record<strin… (the whole schema: discover_operations with names) |  | Leave it out (an undo states the main-language value src hashes). |

Example inputs:

```json
{"at":{"page":"be000742-3ff0-4d5e-a56b-6c728a8851f7"},"locale":"en","pointer":"/tree/nodes/d0166a12/text","value":"We give shape to spaces that balance light, matter and proportion."}
```
```json
{"at":{"page":"be000742-3ff0-4d5e-a56b-6c728a8851f7"},"locale":"en","pointer":"/head/description","value":"Archiplan, architecture and interior design studio in Rome."}
```

{"at":{"component":"site-header"},"locale":"en","pointer":"/tree/nodes/k3m9x2pq/text","value":"Projects"}
